chunks: Sahl, from al-Sindy ibn al-Rabi', from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs, brother of Murazim, from al-Mufaddal who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about something from the Attributes (of God). So he said: Do not exceed what is in the Quran.

key_terms.الصِّفَة: The divine Attributes — referring to the theological discussion of God's names and qualities
key_terms.الْقُرْآن: The Quran — the authoritative boundary and source for all permissible theological discourse
key_terms.لَا تَجَاوَزْ: Do not exceed/go beyond — a prohibition against speculative elaboration on divine attributes beyond the Quranic text

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Kazim say about discussing the attributes of God?
ai.summary: Al-Mufaddal, a close companion of Imam al-Kazim (peace be upon him), asked the Imam about the divine Attributes (sifat). The Imam's concise response — 'Do not exceed what is in the Quran' — establishes a foundational principle of Shia theology: that proper discussion of God's attributes must remain bounded by what God has revealed about Himself in the Quran, prohibiting speculative theological elaboration beyond Quranic revelation. This hadith appears in the chapter on the impermissibility of describing God with attributes other than those He has described Himself with, reflecting the Imami position of 'tafwid' (delegation/restraint) in theological discourse about the Divine.

en.hubeali: Sahl, from Al Sindy Bin Al Rabi’e, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs a brother of Marazim, from Al Mufazzal who said,
‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about something from the Attributes. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not exceed what is in the Quran’.
en.sarwar: 7. Sahl has narrated from al-Sindi ibn al-Rabi‘ from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs, brother of Marazim from al-Mufaddal who has said
the “I asked Imam abu al-Hassan (a.s.) about certain matters of the attributes (of Allah) and the Imam said, “Do not exceed what is in the holy Quran.”
